epic.intent:
## Outcome

Turn execution mistakes into durable, reviewable prevention instead of losing them in attempt history. Rejection reasons remain tied to the exact ticket and attempt and are injected into the next retry packet automatically. Every successfully completed sprint produces exactly one idempotent learning Kanban card after checkpoint advance. The same orchestrator claims and delegates that queued card before polling ordinary work in the next sprint, without blocking sprint advancement.

The card receives an immutable evidence snapshot containing rejected attempts, failed or reconciled attempts, failed row and acceptance checks, and the sprint retro's `wentPoorly` and `actions`. Its worker must disposition every item as a reusable learning, a duplicate, or sprint-specific noise; deduplicate the reusable items; propose scoped learning records for workers and/or orchestrators; and add repository guardrails such as tests, lint rules, documentation or skills when those are the stronger prevention.

Repository edits run on isolated learning branches/worktrees rooted at the completed sprint increment. A multi-repository sprint may produce one guarded branch per affected repository under the same card. The card reaches Ready for review without blocking the next sprint. Human approval preflights and integrates every branch, then publishes the learning records; a conflict, failed integration, or kick-back publishes nothing. Published records are selected by role and path into future worker packets and orchestrator context. A Learnings surface shows provenance and applicability and lets a person retire or replace stale guidance.

## Confirmed decisions

- Evidence sources: rejections, failures/reconciliations, failed row and acceptance checks, and retro `wentPoorly`/`actions`.
- Codification may create first-class learning records and any justified repository guardrails.
- Generation happens only after the sprint checkpoint advances; it is non-blocking.
- The same orchestrator picks up the generated card.
- Learning records activate only on human approval.
- Guardrail work is isolated from ongoing sprint work.
- One card may span every affected repository in a repository-folder project.
- People can inspect, retire and replace published learnings.

## Non-goals

- No automatic approval or checkpoint authority for agents.
- No learning becomes active while its card is merely In progress or Ready for review.
- No mutation of historical attempts, reports or retros to retrofit conclusions.
- No checkpoint gate: the next sprint may proceed while codification is being reviewed.
- No blanket conversion of every failure into permanent guidance; the card must justify or dismiss each source item.
- No direct edits to built-in Dark Mechanicus facts in another installation; repository guardrails stay in the project repositories the sprint affected.

## Standards

Each work ticket lists and runs its targeted tests. The sprint acceptance node runs the project's Definition of Done once on the combined increment. No additional tests-first or Fireguard requirement is added by this plan.

## Explicit feature-first recovery directive
The person directed: stop building test infrastructure and build the feature. Consolidate all existing feature implementation/UI/lifecycle tickets into the active sprint, eliminate the intermediate foundation-only checkpoint, and run the complete Definition of Done once at end-to-end feature acceptance. Already accepted ownership/PTY fixes and original failure records remain; no failed test is relabeled passed. Unresolved historical latency work DM-783 and unstarted scheduling detour DM-792 are optional/deferred and must not consume feature execution. The completed DM-791 NO-GO remains historical evidence with its limitations; it does not mandate an endless diagnostic loop or block the separately specified product tickets. This explicitly supersedes prior recovery proposals that made proving the unrecorded old pathological phase or adding a resource-policy ticket a prerequisite to feature implementation. All original feature outcomes, real Electron evidence, test limits, coverage thresholds and human authority controls remain unchanged. No new probes, fixture frameworks or test-only work are authorized before feature delivery; feature tests use existing harnesses and each ticket's Tests section. Save/adoption is still the execution boundary.

successCriteria.text: A rejected ticket's retry packet identifies every earlier rejected attempt with its actionable reasons, review notes and provenance, so a replacement worker does not rely on the orchestrator manually copying the WHY.

After each successful sprint checkpoint advance, exactly one queued learning card is linked to that run and sprint, contains a complete immutable snapshot of all configured learning sources, and is surfaced for the same orchestrator to claim before ordinary next-sprint polling without blocking the run.

A learning-card worker can disposition every source item, submit deduplicated role/path-scoped learning records, and produce isolated guardrail commits rooted at the completed sprint increment for one or several affected repositories; ordinary Kanban cards keep their current behavior.

Approving a learning card recoverably integrates every declared guardrail branch and publishes its learning records only after all integrations pass; conflict, crash recovery and kick-back paths never leave active records claiming guardrails that were not integrated.

Future worker packets and orchestrator context contain only applicable active learning records with evidence provenance, while bounded selection prevents the guidance from overwhelming the execution packet.

A person can inspect each learning's source sprint, tickets, attempts and checks, see its roles and paths, and retire or replace it; portable export/import preserves cards, records, lifecycle state and integration recovery across repository and database storage modes.

bundle.rationale:
## Evidence inspected

- `rejectAttempt` already persists actionable `reasons` and `notes` on an attempt (`src/core/services/attempts.ts`), but `executionPacket` carries only the current ticket and accepted predecessors; the next worker does not receive earlier rejection decisions.
- The shipped `orchestrator.retry-escalation` fact tells the orchestrator to copy reasons manually, confirming the handoff is procedural rather than enforced.
- Sprint retros already record `wentPoorly` and `actions`, and reports/search preserve them, but no first-class learning lifecycle exists.
- Kanban already supports authorized launch/claim and human-only approval, but ordinary cards work directly on the checked-out branch.
- Knowledge facts already support role/event/topic/path selection and token budgets, but pushed context is orchestrator-only and facts are unmanaged Markdown files.
- The completed SPACE scorecards epic established corrective retrospectives; this epic extends that loop rather than replacing it.

## Selected design

Use immutable evidence plus human-reviewed publication. Rejections reach retries immediately as exact attempt history. A successful checkpoint advance atomically creates and queues one special learning card from a deterministic evidence snapshot. The same orchestrator claims it as its next procedural action, but the run and next sprint remain unblocked. The worker classifies every source item and may propose both scoped learning records and concrete repository guardrails. Guardrail work uses branches/worktrees rooted at the completed increment. Human approval prepares and recoverably integrates all repositories before one final transaction publishes records and completes the card. Active records reuse bounded role/path/event selection for future worker packets and orchestrator context. Humans can later retire or replace records without deleting history.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Prompt-only copying of rejection reasons:** cheap, but it is the current failure mode and remains dependent on orchestrator memory.
- **Publish a fact immediately on every rejection:** fast, but turns one reviewer's local observation into unreviewed permanent authority and amplifies noise.
- **Make codification a next-sprint plan ticket or checkpoint gate:** would guarantee ordering, but the person explicitly chose post-completion, non-blocking Kanban work.
- **Use ordinary Kanban direct-checkout edits:** conflicts with the next sprint and violates the selected isolation requirement.
- **Activate records at Ready for review:** lets unreviewed or malicious guidance affect agents before the person approves it.
- **One card per repository:** simplifies Git integration but fragments the requested single sprint-wide synthesis and can publish inconsistent subsets.

## Dependency graph and critical path

The shared contract is first. Lifecycle services and the evidence collector then proceed in parallel. The service unlocks portable records and context delivery; service plus evidence unlock generated-card creation. Card generation unlocks structured isolated submission. Submission then splits into the Git integration engine and core approval state machine; the desktop coordinator joins them. Kanban review UI and Learnings management UI proceed once their underlying APIs exist. Guidance follows stable command/workflow behavior. The end-to-end ticket joins persistence, delivery, approval, both UIs and guidance before the acceptance node. Critical path: contract → service/evidence → generation → submission → Git/core approval → desktop approval → guidance → end-to-end → acceptance.

## Risks and mitigations

- **The next sprint can start before the card is approved.** This is confirmed behavior, not a hidden guarantee. Same-ticket retries still receive raw rejection WHY immediately; cross-ticket codified guidance activates only after approval.
- **Cross-repository Git is not atomic.** Prepare every result before moving targets, persist expected old/new heads, use compare-and-swap updates, record each applied repository, recover from actual Git truth, and publish records only after all heads verify.
- **Self-reinforcing bad guidance or prompt injection.** Evidence and worker output remain task data; schemas contain no capability/approval fields; human approval is mandatory; applicability is bounded; management can retire/replace.
- **Context overload.** Deduplicate, scope by role/path/event, impose a separate budget, and expose omissions.
- **Stale guidance.** Preserve provenance and replacement chains and provide human retirement/replacement controls.
- **Legacy/storage drift.** Version strict portable records, migrate forward only, keep optional fields absent on older records, and test repo/database round trips.

## Verification strategy

Each work ticket runs only its targeted tests and typecheck when it changes types. The dedicated lifecycle ticket proves assembled single- and multi-repository behavior and captures real Electron evidence. The sprint acceptance node runs the project's Definition of Done exactly once on the combined increment and checks every ticket through a covering criterion. No additional tests-first or Fireguard requirement is imposed by this plan.

The sanctioned retro redraft moves it and its dependents to Sprint 2. DM-720/DM-724 remain accepted in Sprint 1. This is a proposed recovery checkpoint, not a delivered user feature. It adds one full acceptance/report/human checkpoint cost. The person explicitly selected the foundation-only recovery checkpoint and instructed the orchestrator to prepare its draft correction because human sprint-edit controls are intentionally restricted. Sprint 1 goal, exit criteria and DM-719 artifacts are aligned to accepted DM-720/DM-724 only. ## Tests and scope
Each implementation ticket writes/runs its existing Tests section against feature behavior. This node runs the full project Definition of Done once on the completed combined feature increment: npm run lint; npm run typecheck; npm test (including its Fireguard UNIT phase); npm run coverage; npm run deadcode; npm run build. The original DM-719 full gate remains FAILED. ## Verified source and intended change
- src/main/git/learningIntegration.ts: heldRefTransaction currently sends abort at 120000ms independently of awaited work; refTransaction nests symbolic-HEAD and branch transactions; applyTarget performs the canonical read-tree. Replace independent premature lock release with one coordinated transition deadline/cancellation and safe containment ordering. Hold both native locks until the owned checkout write actually stops, including rejection/cancellation/timeout paths; prevent starting further canonical work after cancellation. Settle owned ref-process cleanup honestly too.
- src/main/git/runner.ts: GitRunRequest already supplies signal and onExit. Its documented result rejects before the write has necessarily stopped; only onExit is the actual exit barrier. WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS is 120000 and kill grace 2000ms; the internal next-write queue does not contain the write for this caller. Consume the existing signal/onExit contract rather than treating rejection as exit. No production runner rewrite or new process/ownership framework.
- src/main/git/learningIntegration.test.ts: extend the existing native consumer fixtures. Preserve every existing case and bound.

## Invariants / non-goals
Retain exact expected-old CAS, symbolic HEAD identity, safe index/worktree handling, live registered preparation checks, source ownership, deterministic locks, persist-before-first-change, awaited exact receipt replay, null/empty sources and partial/repeated recovery. Existing finite write/kill/cleanup bounds remain; waiting for already-owned containment is not permission for new work or infinite cleanup.
